scope: Correct water appearance in two illustrative previews only; shallow/deep are represented by entire grid cells. No runtime/mechanics changes.
prompts:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: corrected tactical battlefield illustration, same 1448x1086 image.
Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET.
USER CORRECTION: SHALLOW WATER IS A SEPARATE TERRAIN TILE. Every shallow-water tile occupies ONE WHOLE gameplay grid cell. Deep water is another whole-cell tile type. The previous natural shoreline depth gradient was incorrect.
ONLY EDIT THE WATER AREA. Lock all land tiles, six characters, traps/acid/fire/rune, bridge/blocks, camera, UI/text/background and pixel art finish as closely as possible. Preserve the current muted palette and the modest details.
CRITICAL DRAWING RULES:
1. The whole battlefield uses one consistent isometric lattice. Water surfaces MUST now show the SAME diamond cell grid, same diamond width/height and orientation as immediately adjacent land cells. Each tile is a full rhombus with 4 straight pixel-stepped sides. Both grid directions must continue from existing floor cells across the water, without changing angle, spacing or scale. No little decorative diamonds inside tiles.
2. SHALLOW TILE: the ENTIRE diamond is light muted blue-green water (#62887E/#86AAA8) over a faintly visible sandy/stone riverbed (#978971/#A6967B tinted by water). The whole-cell floor plane is subtly visible through the water, not just a little rock. One tiny angular submerged stone may appear on one shallow cell, but no scattering. Use 2-3 broad flat pixel clusters.
3. DEEP TILE: the ENTIRE diamond is darker blue-teal (#315361/#3E6570/#527F87) with NO visible bed. Only one or two short angular pixel reflection strokes per several tiles.
4. The shallow/deep division coincides EXACTLY with the straight shared edge of two neighboring full diamonds. Sharp meaningful change of material at that edge. Shallow tiles can directly adjoin deep tiles in any grid direction. A thin subdued grid seam makes each whole water cell countable.
5. NO partial-cell shallows, shoreline ribbons, rings around rocks, organic depth patches, smooth depth gradients, diagonal internal splits or extra subdivision. NO rock stepping-stones or raised cubes masquerading as shallow water. Both are flat WATER tiles at the same surface level, with different visible depth.
6. Keep overall water region recognizable from input; if needed straighten its outline minimally to whole existing grid cells. Tile readability takes precedence over preserving the old wavy interior patches. Do not increase terrain detail.
Show discrete water terrain cells as actual gameplay tiles, integrated into the existing battlefield. This is an illustration only, not an implementation. No text labels, legends, swatches, comparison panels or new HUD.
FORD SPECIFIC: replace the entire continuous river with a connected sequence of FULL DIAMOND water cells at the land grid scale. Near the downstream/front side of the existing bridge put TWO ADJACENT complete shallow-water cells side by side so they form an unmistakable whole-tile shallow crossing. Further upstream show ONE additional complete shallow-water cell beside a deep cell. Make the remaining river cells deep blue-teal. Extend the exact ground lattice over the water: no curving bright shoreline border anywhere. Preserve the bridge and its location. The shallow pair must have full diamond outlines and visible bed through the entire water tile.
